key_concepts: Robert Boyle studied the relationship between gas volume and pressure in 1662
At constant temperature, gas volume decreases as pressure increases
Boyle’s Law states that volume is inversely proportional to pressure at constant temperatu
Kinetic Molecular Theory explains that gas molecules exert pressure on container walls
Applying pressure moves gas molecules closer together, decreasing volume
Decreased volume increases collisions among molecules and container walls, increasing pres
Boyle’s Law is mathematically expressed as P1V1 = P2V2
Common pressure units include Pascal, atmosphere, torr, and mm Hg
Pressure conversions include 1 atm = 760 torr = 760 mm Hg and 1 atm = 101,325 Pa
Common volume units include cubic meter, cubic centimeter, liter, and milliliter
Boyle’s Law applies only when temperature remains constant
Real-life applications include car tire inflation and syringes
